blocks.text: A lot of a recruiter's day goes to admin, not to conversations with candidates. Email, notes, scheduling and tracker updates fill the gaps between calls. An AI assistant for recruiters can help with that work, but only if it works in the apps you already open. This page shows where the time goes, what a realistic day looks like with Lazur, and where you need to be careful with candidate data.
Where recruiter admin time goes

Recruiter-only time studies are scarce. Most public numbers come from surveys of HR leaders, or from telemetry on all office workers. So read the figures below as direction, not as a timetable for your week. SmartRecruiters ran a 2024 survey of 533 HR and talent professionals at midsize companies in the US, UK and Australia. It found that 45% of talent-acquisition leaders spend over half their working hours on admin tasks. The survey says those tasks could be automated through AI.

That group is talent-acquisition leaders, not recruiters. Read it as a close neighbor, not an exact match for your week. The other figures come from different years and methods, so none of them lines up cleanly with the others.

rows: 45% of talent-acquisition leaders spend over half their working hours on admin
Almost two hours a day on admin, from a sample of 53 in-house recruiters
117 emails received per day by the average worker, across all office roles
8.8 hours a week on email for the heaviest 25% of email users
blocks.caption: Four public figures. Each uses its own method, so compare them with care.

blocks.text: The 2015 number is the oldest one here, and the weakest. HR Review reported Cornerstone OnDemand research saying in-house recruiters spend almost two hours a day on administrative tasks. The article cites 53 in-house recruiters and does not link to the original study. Use it to see that admin has long competed with sourcing. Do not use it as a benchmark for 2026.

Interruptions can set the pace of a recruiter's day. Microsoft's 2025 WorkLab report says people are interrupted every 2 minutes during core work hours. The interruptions come from meetings, emails or chats. Microsoft also counts 275 interruptions a day on a 24-hour basis. The page says those two figures use different bases, so do not add them together.

Most of the lost time is not typing. It is finding things. You look for the candidate's last reply, the right template, the interview panel and the approved pay range. Each lookup breaks the thread you were in. That is the part worth shrinking.
Why email takes so much of the morning

Email is where many recruiting days start. Microsoft's 2025 figures say the average worker receives 117 emails a day. Those numbers cover knowledge workers in general, not recruiters, so your count may be higher or lower. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index adds another split. The average worker spends 57% of their time communicating and 43% creating.

Microsoft Research looked at this pattern in a 2016 CHI study. It tracked 40 information workers over 12 workdays, using computer logging, biosensors and daily surveys. Longer daily time on email was linked to lower perceived productivity and higher measured stress. The page gives no hour-per-day cutoff, so do not set one from memory.

Batching is the habit most people try first. Check mail at set times instead of all day. It helps when you control when you look. It does not help when a hiring manager messages you in the middle of a debrief. That gap is where a voice assistant can help, because you can ask a question without leaving the call notes or the candidate page.
Voice assistant for recruiters: a realistic day

Here is a day that could look like yours. The times are a plan, not a log. The point is where Lazur fits. You talk to it when your hands are busy, or when you need an answer about the screen in front of you. You do not need to talk to it all day.

Start with the inbox. Hold ⌥ ⌘ over the first unread threads and ask which ones need an answer today. Lazur answers out loud from what is on screen. It does not sort or open the mail for you. You still read the thread, and you still decide what gets a reply.

Dictation saves the most time right after a call. Hold fn and speak your notes. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Add candidate names, team names and role titles to your personal dictionary first. That saves you from fixing the same spelling in every note.

Snippets and clipboard slots help with the parts you repeat. A closing line for candidates, a standard decline note or a link to your scheduling page can each live in a snippet. Pick the ones you type most often and start there.
Recruiter email assistant on Mac: how Lazur works in Gmail

Lazur reads the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about what you see. In a Gmail thread open in Chrome, you can ask what the candidate wants, or whether they answered your question about start dates. Lazur answers out loud. The answer comes from the page, so ask about the page you have open.

Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. This helps with small buttons in a tracker or an email client. Ask where the Send button is, and Lazur circles it. You press it yourself. The decision to send stays with you.

For how-to questions, ask Lazur to walk you through it. Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. This is slower than doing it yourself. It helps when a setting is buried, or when you have not used a feature in a while.

Drafting is where a voice assistant pays back quickly. Ask for a short reply in plain words, such as a note that asks the candidate to confirm a time. Lazur types the draft into the reply box. Read it, change any names, times or figures, and send it yourself. The draft is a starting point, not a final email.
Candidate data and your employer's rules

Candidate data is personal data. A CV, a phone number, interview notes and an offer figure all count. Your employer decides what can go into an AI tool. Check the policy before you use Lazur on a candidate thread. If the policy says no, do not use it on that thread, even for a quick question.

Lazur's privacy notes say it listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Those are product statements. They are not a compliance certificate, and they do not replace your employer's rules.

Some roles carry stricter duties. Recruiters who place people in health, legal or financial work may handle data under extra rules. If you work in a regulated field, follow your employer's rules on that data. Ask your data protection or HR team before you add any new tool to your work.
Recruiting tools on Mac: LinkedIn Recruiter and Greenhouse

If you source on LinkedIn Recruiter, know what its help page covers. LinkedIn says you reach LinkedIn Recruiter and Recruiter Lite through the Recruiter mobile app. Only iOS 14 or later can upgrade to the newest version. The page does not mention a desktop or Mac app. Confirm with LinkedIn or your admin before you plan your Mac setup around it.

Greenhouse has a Recruiting Chrome extension for CRM. Its support article says it is available on Core, Plus and Pro subscription tiers. It is for users with Job Admin or higher who can manage CRM and prospects. The article does not name supported browsers or operating systems, so ask your admin to confirm Mac and Chrome support first.

Lazur does not connect to LinkedIn Recruiter or Greenhouse. It is not an add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. What it can do is read the page you have open, point at the field you need, and draft text for it. Think of it as a second pair of eyes on the page, not as a connector.
Outlook for Mac: legacy versus new Outlook

Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes from October 2026. Exchange Web Services retires on 1 October 2026. Microsoft also says over 95% of Microsoft 365 users have already moved to the new Outlook for Mac. That date has passed. If you still open the old app, switch now.

If your company runs Exchange On-Premises, the timeline is different. Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac keeps working there until 9 October 2029, with security updates and best-effort technical support. Check which mail system your company runs before you change anything. Your IT team can tell you in one message.
Mistakes to avoid with an AI assistant for recruiters

items: Pasting full CVs into an AI tool before you check your employer's rules.
Sending a drafted reply without reading it. Names, dates and role titles can drift.
Dictating feedback about a candidate and skipping the review step before it reaches a hiring manager.
Holding the shortcut on a screen that shows other people's data. Lazur only looks while you hold the key, but you choose the screen.
Asking for a guide, then clicking ahead. Lazur waits for each click, so let it set the pace.

blocks.text: A quieter mistake is treating the first answer as the final one. Lazur can misread a small element, especially a tiny icon. Ask a follow-up, or ask it to point at the element before you act. Then check the result on screen.
A worked example: answering a candidate about pay

Say a candidate replies to an offer email and asks whether the salary range can move. You open the thread in Gmail in Chrome. You hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the candidate is asking. Lazur answers out loud from the page. You then ask for a short draft that says you will check with the hiring manager and reply by a set date.

Lazur types the draft into the reply box. You then check every figure against the offer sheet your team approved. You edit the wording, and you press Send yourself. The whole loop stays in your hands. Lazur speeds up the reading and the first draft, nothing more.
How to start with Lazur this week

items: Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) and open it on your Mac.
Open one candidate thread in Gmail or Apple Mail, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask what needs an answer.
Hold fn after your next call and dictate the notes. Check the names before you save.
Add candidate names, team names and role titles to your personal dictionary.
Read your employer's AI policy before you use Lazur on candidate data.

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for recruiters that works inside Gmail?
faq.answer: Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It works in any app, including Gmail open in Chrome, because it reads the screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘. It is not an add-in for Gmail, and it does not send mail for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons or send my replies?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides, points, explains, answers out loud, drafts and types text. You make every click, including Send.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur with LinkedIn Recruiter on my Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur has no partnership with LinkedIn, and it does not connect to LinkedIn Recruiter. LinkedIn's help page describes a mobile app for Recruiter and does not mention a Mac app. Check with your admin before you plan around it.

faq.question: Does Lazur store what I say or the screens I show it?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and are not stored, according to Lazur's privacy notes. Your employer's policy still decides what you can share.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. There is a free trial with no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. Check the pricing page for current plans.
